title: Contain the failure before resuming the run
description: Inject a realistic failure, choose a response and authority scope, then inspect the relative blast radius, surviving path, and evidence required for recovery.

authorities.label: Read-only capability
authorities.detail: The run can retrieve approved data but cannot create an external effect.

authorities.label: Bounded write capability
authorities.detail: The run can write only named resources within explicit values and expiration.

authorities.label: Broad write capability
authorities.detail: The run can modify many resources, so one bad decision can cross task boundaries.

responses.label: Keep running and retry
responses.detail: Preserve authority and let the same path continue after the observed failure.

responses.label: Isolate and reconcile
responses.detail: Pause the affected worker or tool, compare durable state, and resume only from confirmed evidence.

responses.label: Halt and revoke
responses.detail: Stop the run, revoke delegated grants, quarantine suspect context, and require accountable review.

responses.label: Recover from durable journal
responses.detail: Lease the task to a healthy coordinator and reconstruct state from committed events.

scenarios.label: Retrieved instruction attempts data egress
scenarios.detail: A document returned by search contains instructions to ignore policy and send protected data elsewhere.
scenarios.signal: Untrusted content requests a new destination and a capability outside the user task.
scenarios.survivingPath: Treat retrieved text as data, quarantine the record, and rebuild context from approved provenance.
scenarios.recoveryEvidence: No egress call occurred, delegated grants are revoked, and the source record is quarantined.

scenarios.label: Tool timeout leaves write outcome unknown
scenarios.detail: The runtime sent a write, lost the response, and cannot tell whether the external system committed it.
scenarios.signal: The attempt timed out after request transmission and has no authoritative receipt.
scenarios.survivingPath: Query by idempotency key, classify the outcome, and retry only a confirmed non-effect.
scenarios.recoveryEvidence: Authoritative state shows exactly zero or one effect associated with the original key.

scenarios.label: Two workers receive the same leased task
scenarios.detail: A delayed acknowledgement causes the coordinator to redeliver work while the first worker is still active.
scenarios.signal: Two attempt IDs claim the same task lease and target the same idempotency key.
scenarios.survivingPath: Fence the old lease, suppress duplicate effects, and retain one authoritative owner.
scenarios.recoveryEvidence: One live lease remains and the effect ledger contains at most one committed write.

scenarios.label: Coordinator fails after workers finish
scenarios.detail: Workers produced results, but the supervisor stopped before recording the parent task outcome.
scenarios.signal: The parent lease expired while durable child-completion events remain unconsumed.
scenarios.survivingPath: Elect a new owner, replay committed events, and avoid repeating confirmed child work.
scenarios.recoveryEvidence: The rebuilt parent state references every child attempt and reaches one terminal outcome.

scenarios.label: A false fact enters long-term memory
scenarios.detail: A low-trust tool result was summarized as an authoritative customer preference and reused later.
scenarios.signal: The memory record lacks source provenance and conflicts with a newer authoritative record.
scenarios.survivingPath: Quarantine dependent memories, rebuild from source records, and rerun affected evaluations.
scenarios.recoveryEvidence: Conflicting records are resolved, derived memories are invalidated, and impacted runs are identified.
